answer: A walnut commit-reveal stops copied work from passing as original. Before starting a job, the alias posts a hash of its work plan to the public ledger under a walnut token only it holds. The commit, the reveal, and the delivery meet at one vertex in the ledger, so all three can be checked. The alias must reveal the plan inside a 24-hour horizon or the job pays nothing. Three mismatched commits in 30 days suspend the alias for 30 days and mark it publicly so requesters skip it. A farm copying one plan across many aliases cannot post matching commits in time.
